summary: Server-only results of the 'mon' (EocServerMonitor, a debug monitor) request mon::InvalidInteractableRequestComponent. Registered in App::InitServer (bg3.exe+0x11EFBA0, size 0x10, align 0x10); no system of bg3.exe or of the Toolkit DLLs reads or writes it (the monitor implementation is not shipped), so only the destructor gives the shape: an Array of 48-byte elements that start with a string. Never seen alive.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: destructor bg3.exe+0x11F15D0 (jumped to from bg3.exe+0x11F15C0, registered by bg3.exe+0x11EFBA0) walks the elements with stride 0x30 and frees a 24-byte game string at +0 of each (capacity u32 at +0x14 > 0xF -> free; resets size +0x10 = 0, capacity = 0xF). Probably a name/description of the invalid interactable.

fields.name: field_18
fields.evidence: trivially destructible remainder of the 0x30-byte element; nothing in bg3.exe writes or reads it. macOS destructor (bg3_macos_x64+0x25DC0B0) uses stride 0x28 (libc++ string + 16 bytes): the Windows tail is 8 bytes longer, so the remainder holds something 8-aligned that differs in padding - unknown.

fields.name: Results
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x11F15D0: Array{ptr +0, capacity u32 +8, size u32 +0xC}; element stride 0x30 and its string member from the destructor loop; registry size 16 (server row).

open_questions: The 24 bytes after the string in each element (no producer exists in bg3.exe or the Toolkit DLLs; the monitor module that fills it is not shipped).
Whether the macOS stride 0x28 vs Windows 0x30 hides a 16-aligned member (e.g. a vec4/__m128) in the tail.
status_reason: no live or captured instance: needs a situation that creates it
second_pass: Cannot be settled from code: the second pass found no producer or consumer anywhere - bg3.exe has only the type registration (App::CreateECS -> bg3.exe+0x11EExxx), the static type-name initialiser and the component ops; the macOS build has only ComponentOps/ComponentSignals/destructor instantiations (macos_index.py names '<mon::' lists just the eight mon types) and the Toolkit DLLs mention them only in App::AddGlobalSwitchesToOptionDialog. The shapes from the creator/destructor stand; the members stay unknown.
